title: The data engineer’s role in the model lifecycle

videos.script: Four lessons of programs, and every one of them worked. Not one of them could run in production. {{four}} They read the database from whatever folder they were started in. They decided their own dates. Nothing checked what they read. And nothing wrote down what they made. {{wrong}} A model's life is a loop. Data becomes features, features train a model, the model is checked, deployed, watched, and trained again. {{loop}} The modeller owns one stop on that loop. The platform owns the rest. {{owns}} This lesson turns the scripts into a pipeline. Four steps, each with a file in and a file out. {{steps}} One refuses labels that are not finished. One refuses a dataset with a negative recency in it. One writes down exactly which data a model came from. {{refuse}} Then the quietest failure in the whole lifecycle. The same model, given the same members, with features computed by somebody else's code. {{skew}} Nothing errors. A hundred and sixty probabilities move. {{moves}} By the end you will know which parts of a model are yours. And what to ask for before you take them on. {{end}}
